g.text: GHSA-22jm-h49p-29qw Experimental tasks were not tied to the session that created them
GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk has cross-client data leak via shared server/transport
GHSA-46jr-4wx8-v453 One HTTP request within the default size limit could exhaust server memory during
GHSA-6qxp-vccf-f47h OAuth client could send credentials to an authorization server chosen by the MCP
GHSA-8r9q-7v3j-jr4g Anthropic's MCP TypeScript SDK has a ReDoS vulnerability
GHSA-f897-62hf-6gxq HTTP server transports and handlers did not limit request body size or JSON-RPC batch
GHSA-6prh-2h8m-c8cw HTTP client transports and OAuth requests followed cross-origin redirects and re-sent
GHSA-rvq5-wwqv-78pq Server bearer authentication accepted tokens issued for another service
Code that stays exposed after upgrading
One McpServer/Server instance connect()ed to many transports (server-to-client messages can cross clients)
> const server = new McpServer({ name: "demo", version: "1.0.0" });
fix: Build a new McpServer inside the request/session handler, or pass a factory to createMcpHandler().
Patched SDKs throw ALREADY_CONNECTED on the second connect().
HTTP transport created once at module scope and shared by all clients (responses can reach the wrong client)
> const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({ sessionIdGenerator: undefined });
fix: Create the transport per request (stateless) or per session (sessionIdGenerator set). Patched SDKs
reject the shared pattern at runtime, so this is also an upgrade blocker.
Bundled OAuth provider without expectedIssuer still sends credentials to any authorization server the MCP
fix: Upgrade to @modelcontextprotocol/sdk >=1.31.0 or @modelcontextprotocol/client >=2.2.0 and pass
requireBearerAuth/verifyBearerToken without expectedResource accepts tokens issued for other services
fix: Upgrade (sdk >=1.32.0 / server >=2.3.0), pass expectedResource: new URL('<your MCP URL>') AND return
AuthInfo.resource from verifyAccessToken(). Or check `aud` yourself in verifyAccessToken().
redirectPolicy: 'follow' re-enables cross-origin redirects that leak headers, session ids and token-request
> const t2 = new StreamableHTTPClientTransport(new URL(UPSTREAM), { authProvider: upstream, redirectPolicy:
fix: Remove redirectPolicy: 'follow' and configure the final URL directly.
1 SDK dependency, 8 vulnerable matches, 5 code findings (1 source file scanned)
